messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The model that only observes answers (MLP-A) performs significantly worse than the model that observes all three sources of information (MLP-IQA) on the COCOQA dataset." -- cites: E2 (Section Table 8): quote "MLP-A 70.3 31.7 26.6"; E2 (Section Table 8): quote "MLP-IQA 93.1 78.3 75.9"
2. "The model that observes only images and answers (MLP-IA) performs better than the model that only observes answers (MLP-A) but worse than the model that observes all three sources of information (MLP-IQA) on the COCOQA dataset." -- cites: E2 (Section Table 8): quote "MLP-IA 73.4 73.3 60.7"; E2 (Section Table 8): quote "MLP-IQA 93.1 78.3 75.9"
3. "The model that observes all three sources of information (images, questions, and answers) performs the best on the COCOQA dataset when considering the combined accuracy of identifying irrelevant image-question pairs (IU) and irrelevant question-answer pairs (QU)." -- cites: E2 (Section Table 8): quote "MLP-IQA 93.1 78.3 75.9"
4. "The model that only observes answers (MLP-A) attains about the chance-level accuracy on the COCOQA dataset." -- cites: E6 (Section 3.2): quote "The model learns the specific statistics of the candidate answers in the dataset and exploits those. Adding the information about the image (i.e., the row of “I+A”), the machine improves significantly and gets close to the performance when all information is used (62.4% vs. 65.7%)."

Cited evidence:
[E2] (text, Section Table 8, page 15): Table 8: Test accuracy (%) on COCOQA. Method IoU QoU IoU +QoU MLP-A 70.3 31.7 26.6 MLP-IA 73.4 73.3 60.7 MLP-QA 91.5 52.5 51.4 MLP-IQA 93.1 78.3 75.9 Random 25.0 25.0 14.3
[E6] (text, Section 3.2, page 4): Machines ﬁnd shortcuts Table 1 summarizes the performance of the learning models, together with the human studies we performed on a subset of 1,000 triplets (c.f. Sect. 5 for details). There are a few interesting observations. First, in the row of “A” where only the candidate answers (and whether they are right or wrong) are used to train a learning model, the model performs signiﬁcantly better than random guessing and humans (52.9% vs. 25%) — humans will deem each of the answers equally likely without looking at both the image and the question! Note that in this case, the information i in eq. ( 1 ) contains nothing. The model learns the speciﬁc statistics of the candidate answers in the dataset and exploits those. Adding the information about the image (i.e., the row of “I+A”), the machine improves signiﬁcantly and gets close to the performance when all information is used (62.4% vs. 65.7%). There is a weaker correlation between the question and the answers as “Q+A” improves over “A” only modestly. This is expected. In the Visual7W dataset, the decoys are generated by human annotators as plausible answers to the questions without being shown the images — thus, many decoy answers do not have visual groundings. For instance, a question of “what animal is running?” elicits equally likely answers such as “dog”, “tiger”, “lion”, or “cat”, while an image of a dog running in the park will immediately rule out all 3 but the “dog”, see Fig. 1 for a similar example. Thus, the performance of “I+A” implies that many IQA triplets can be solved by object, attribute or concept detection on the image, without understanding the questions. verdicts.reason: The evidence in E2 (Section Table 8) shows that MLP-A has a combined accuracy of 26.6% and MLP-IQA has a combined accuracy of 75.9%. This supports the claim that MLP-A performs significantly worse than MLP-IQA.

The evidence in E2 (Section Table 8) shows that MLP-IA has a combined accuracy of 60.7% and MLP-IQA has a combined accuracy of 75.9%. This supports the claim that MLP-IA performs better than MLP-A but worse than MLP-IQA.
The evidence in E2 (Section Table 8) shows that MLP-IQA has a combined accuracy of 75.9%. This supports the claim that MLP-IQA performs the best.

The evidence in E6 (Section 3.2) discusses the performance of MLP-A and mentions that it performs significantly better than random guessing and humans (52.9% vs. 25%). It does not state that MLP-A attains about the chance-level accuracy. The claim is not supported by the evidence.
